why: GitHub Agentic Workflows compiles every workflow into a lock file that starts the agent with its approval switch off inside a firewall container: 10 of 10 sampled Codex locks and 15 of 15 Copilot locks carry it. Failing those would fail every gh-aw adopter, so a lock file is only a warning (passed with a note). A lock is recognised by what the compiler writes, not by its comment: a .lock.yml name, the generated header, and activation and agent jobs with the agent needing the activation, the shape of all 24 lock files of the corpora. The fail side pastes the header and a roles comment above a plain workflow, which the review showed lowered it to a warning. Whoever skips lock files silently, fails them, or trusts the comment turns one side the wrong colour.
